whatItDoes: Research a niche, write and self-edit the issue against a quality bar, illustrate it, and email it every week. Searches the web, dedupes and ranks the strongest sources, then drafts and grades the issue against a fixed bar, revising once if it falls short, before sending it to your list or this agent's own inbox.
longDescription: Give it a niche and, optionally, a subscriber list. Every week it searches the web, reads the top results, dedupes near-duplicate stories, and keeps the strongest few. `write` (`llm.run`) curates that week's issue with a subject line, intro, and cited sections, and `selfEdit` grades the draft against a fixed quality bar, revising once if it falls short. It illustrates a header image and emails the issue, defaulting to this agent's own demo inbox when no `subscribers` are set. `dryRun` returns a full preview without emailing.
notes:
Click **Use this template**. Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it.

Give it a `niche` (what to write about) and a `newsletterName`. It runs with no setup: given no niche it writes about indie game development and says so in its output. With no `subscribers` set it emails the finished issue to this agent's own Sapiom-hosted demo inbox, so you see a real, inspectable send. Set `subscribers` (a list of emails) to send it to your list instead. Pass `dryRun: true` to write, self-edit, and illustrate the issue and get it back without emailing anyone at all. To run it weekly, attach the `schedule` as a cron trigger on the deployed agent (it defaults to Mondays at 08:00).

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` to trace the whole research → dedupe → write → selfEdit → illustrate → deliver flow (capabilities stubbed, delivery skipped), or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
